How to choose a blockchain development company

Blockchain development can mean smart contracts, wallet flows, APIs, nodes, indexers, security, account abstraction, cross-chain infrastructure or enterprise architecture. Define the layer before shortlisting providers.
Some providers build complete applications. Others provide APIs, RPC access, indexing, account abstraction or infrastructure. Match the company to the work package.
If the project controls assets, separate engineering from independent audit, monitoring and incident response. Security should be planned before mainnet deployment.
Check EVM, Solana, L2, appchain or enterprise-ledger experience, plus wallet, custody, KYC, payment and data integrations for the target use case.
Tokenization projects need legal, compliance, custody and lifecycle workflows around the blockchain layer. A good developer should understand where code ends and operations begin.
Compare delivery evidence, not just technology lists

Give each shortlisted team the same small workflow: connect a wallet, submit a transaction, display its status and reconcile the result. Ask which parts they build, which services they integrate and which responsibilities stay with your team.
System diagram showing contracts, backend, wallet, RPC, indexer and external dependencies.
Is every dependency assigned to an owner and included or excluded explicitly in the quote?
Sandbox flows for user rejection, a pending transaction and a failed transaction.
Does the interface distinguish submission from confirmation without showing false success?
Rebuild displayed state after a missed event or service restart; document chain-specific finality assumptions.
Can the team reconcile application records without double-counting or losing events?
Load test using your expected read/write mix, plus a simulated RPC timeout.
Are response times, errors, retries and usage costs reported for the same workload?
Repository, reproducible build, deployment instructions, configuration inventory and operating runbook.
Can your nominated maintainer deploy the sandbox without the original developer?

Compare first-year cost using the same assumptions: implementation, independent security review where needed, hosting, third-party services, maintenance and migration. A node subscription supplies infrastructure access; it does not replace a contracted application build. Treat untested capabilities as open questions, not confirmed coverage.
